title: Arizona v. Johnson (2009)
key_points: Holding: During a lawful traffic stop, an officer may frisk a passenger if there is reasonable suspicion the passenger is armed and dangerous; suspicion of other crime by the passenger is not required.
officer_notes: Scenario: A passenger in a stopped car wears gang colors, has a police scanner and says he recently left prison for burglary. You frisk him for weapons.
Takeaway: Articulate the armed-and-dangerous facts specific to that passenger.
